question: A ticket-classification schema has a category field defined as an enum of five known categories: billing, technical, shipping, account, and refund. After deployment, roughly 8% of real tickets don't cleanly fit any of these categories, and the model is observed forcing them into the closest (often incorrect) enum value. Which schema change best addresses this?
options: A) Add a sixth hardcoded category called miscellaneous_unclear_ticket_type_pending_manual_review to the existing enum list
B) Lower the required strictness of the tool by setting strict: false so the model is allowed to skip the category field for edge cases
C) Remove the enum constraint entirely and let category be an unconstrained free-text string so the model can write anything that seems to fit
D) Add an "other" enum value alongside a separate free-text detail field so ambiguous tickets can be captured without corrupting the five known categories
correct_answers: D) Add an "other" enum value alongside a separate free-text detail field so ambiguous tickets can be captured without corrupting the five known categories
explanations: A single rigid extra enum value doesn't provide space to capture the actual nuance of each ambiguous ticket, and the six categories are still a closed, non-extensible set with no detail field.
Making the field skippable would produce missing classifications rather than accurate ones, and does nothing to help distinguish or record what the ambiguous tickets actually are.
Removing the enum sacrifices the consistency and downstream queryability that enums provide, and reintroduces the risk of inconsistent free-text values across many tickets.

Correct. The "other" + detail string pattern lets extensible or ambiguous categories be captured accurately without forcing a misclassification into one of the fixed enum values, while still keeping downstream processing structured.
